subject: UTC rollover and partial-day inclusivity for SOC 2 Type II period
messages:
From: Elena Gray <elena.gray@graydonassurance.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: StratusPay Compliance <compliance@stratuspay.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T14:12:00Z
Subject: Clarify clock boundary for Nov Type II window

Hi Jonas / Marissa,

We're preparing the procedures for the November Type II testing and I ran into a timestamp/cutoff question that I want to confirm with you before we request formal evidence. StratusPay's SOC 2 period is 2026-11-01 through 2026-11-30. Two quick items:  

1) Our audit methodology counts a "day" by UTC midnight unless the vendor states otherwise. Does Redwood use UTC to define daily snapshots and the point-in-time cutoffs for evidence you will provide?  

2) If Redwood ingests request timestamps in application-local time (for customers in various regions), are those normalized to UTC before they become part of the stored logs/evidence? If not, we need to understand how you treat events that cross a midnight boundary in local time but land on a different UTC day.

Additionally, a related practical question: for long-running requests (streams or async jobs) that start before midnight and complete after, does your snapshot capture those as-of the UTC cutoff or by request start time?

If you can confirm the canonical timestamp and whether the November 1–30 window should be interpreted as inclusive of 00:00:00 UTC on Nov 1 through 23:59:59 UTC on Nov 30, that would be great. If more convenient, we can set a short call — I'll leave it to you.

Thanks,
Elena Gray
Senior IT Auditor
Graydon Assurance

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Gray <elena.gray@graydonassurance.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, StratusPay Compliance <compliance@stratuspay.com>
Date: 2026-11-06T09:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarify clock boundary for Nov Type II window

Elena — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front, followed by details and what we can produce:  

- Canonical timestamps: Redwood normalizes all event timestamps to UTC at ingestion and stores UTC as the canonical time in our logs and event store.
- Snapshot cutoffs: Our standard audit snapshots are taken at 00:00:00 UTC. For the November 2026 period that would be inclusive from 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z through 2026-11-30T23:59:59Z (i.e., full UTC days).
- Long-running requests: Evidence is based on final logged events. If an event recording the completion of a request occurs after the UTC cutoff it will not be counted in the earlier snapshot; transactions are included only if the completion event timestamp is <= cutoff. For streaming/ongoing sessions we provide separate session manifests where we mark partials.

What we can supply to make your work easier:  
1) A small sample CSV demonstrating source timestamps (raw), the canonical UTC stored value, and the rule we apply for rollover normalization (attached: timestamp-mapping-sample.csv).
2) A draft bridge letter that explicitly states the UTC-based snapshot policy and how we treat in-flight/long-running operations (attached: bridge-letter-draft.docx).
3) If you prefer, a one-hour call to walk through examples for US and APAC customer records.

I'm cc'ing Karthik (logs and ingestion) and Marissa (SOC 2 program) for visibility; they'll help if you need any raw extracts. Let me know which specific sample dates/times you want and we'll pull them.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Director, Trust & Security
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Gray <elena.gray@graydonassurance.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, StratusPay Compliance <compliance@stratuspay.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T16:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarify clock boundary for Nov Type II window

Thanks Jonas — that helps a lot. A couple of follow-ups so we can define our sampling approach:  

- Please provide the CSV sample for two as-of points: 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z and 2026-11-30T23:59:59Z. For each point, include one example record representing a US customer (stored UTC = same as source) and one representing an APAC customer who originally had a local timestamp that rolled over differently.
- For long-running requests: can you confirm whether your logs contain both a request-start and request-complete event with distinct timestamps, or do you rely on a single final event for completion? If both exist, we'll want to see the pair for a representative long-running job.

If you can attach the CSV and the bridge-letter draft, we'll review internally and propose minor wording changes if needed. A quick call tomorrow morning (US) would be fine if you're available.

Regards,
Elena Gray
Graydon Assurance

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Gray <elena.gray@graydonassurance.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, StratusPay Compliance <compliance@stratuspay.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T09:06:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarify clock boundary for Nov Type II window

Elena — attaching the two requested samples and the bridge-letter draft per your note. Quick confirmations inline:  

- CSVs: each row includes raw_source_timestamp, source_timezone, canonical_utc_timestamp (what we store), and a note field where we flag any timezone normalization applied. The samples are for: 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z (US example) and 2026-11-30T23:59:59Z (APAC example where raw local time was 2026-12-01T08:59:59+09:00 but canonicalized to 2026-11-30T23:59:59Z).
- Long-running requests: our tracing pipeline records both request.start and request.complete events (and we index the complete event as the canonical completion timestamp). For audit snapshots we use the request.complete canonical_utc_timestamp to determine inclusion. If a request.start exists without a matching complete before cutoff, the request will not be counted in the earlier snapshot; we include it in a separate "in-flight" manifest and provide the session id and last-seen timestamp.
- Bridge letter: the draft states the audit snapshot boundary (00:00:00 UTC) and describes normalization rules and the in-flight manifest process. Please let us know specific wording edits and we can finalize. We can also push the artifacts into a restricted Drive folder (link below) if you prefer to pull rather than receive attachments.

Drive evidence folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-evidence
DocuSign (bridge letter): DocuSign: 0a1b2c-bridge-letter-signature-request

If that all looks good, we can proceed to push the CSVs for the rest of the sampled dates you may request and finalize the letter. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call later today (US morning) if helpful.

Best regards,
Jonas Weber
Director, Trust & Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: timestamp-mapping-sample.csv (text/csv), bridge-letter-draft.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)
